title: Ph.D. Project: A Novel Compilation-Based Approach for Generating Sparse Tensor Accelerators
problem: Sparse tensor irregularity challenges GPU/NPU acceleration, and current point-wise manual FPGA design methodologies do not scale efficiently across diverse sparse scenarios.
motivation: Sparse tensor computing is widely used in deep learning and scientific computing, making efficient hardware acceleration critical for performance.
method: Proposes a compiler framework with three components: (1) a schedule-primitive-based DSL for sparse accelerator specification; (2) a two-stage mapping mechanism based on sparse meta-operations to flexibly map dataflow to hardware; (3) a heuristic design space exploration strategy guided by workload characteristics to automatically generate high-performance accelerators.
key_novelty: Compiler-driven automatic generation of reconfigurable sparse tensor accelerators using schedule-primitive DSL and sparse meta-operations mapping.
contributions: Schedule-primitive-based DSL for sparse accelerator design specification
Two-stage sparse meta-operations mapping enabling flexible dataflow-to-hardware translation
Heuristic design space exploration strategy guided by workload characteristics
Automatic FPGA sparse accelerator generation reducing manual design effort
primary_theme: Compiler-driven automatic generation of sparse tensor accelerators on FPGA
